# Vendored third-party code (TTS plugin)

`kokoro.min.js` is a self-contained browser ESM bundle produced from upstream
npm packages so the plugin runs offline without a CDN. All bundled code is under
permissive licenses (no copyleft, no non-commercial terms):

| Package | Version | License |
|---|---|---|
| `kokoro-js` | 1.2.1 | Apache-2.0 (see `LICENSE.kokoro-js`) |
| `@huggingface/transformers` (transformers.js) | ^3.5 | Apache-2.0 |
| `onnxruntime-web` | bundled by the above | MIT |
| `phonemizer` | ^1.2 | MIT |

`voices.json` is voice metadata (names, language, gender, quality grade) extracted
from kokoro-js for the voice picker. The 28 shipped voices are English only
(en-us / en-gb); no CC-BY non-English voices are referenced, so no extra
attribution is required.

## What is NOT vendored (fetched once at runtime, then cached in-browser)

To keep the repo lean, the heavy binaries are fetched on first use and cached by
the browser (Cache API / IndexedDB), exactly like the chat model:

- The Kokoro model weights (~86 MB ONNX) from the Apache-2.0 Hugging Face repo
  named in `tts.example.json` (`model`).
- The onnxruntime-web `.wasm` runtime (~11-21 MB) from transformers.js's default
  CDN.

Neither carries user text off the machine - they are public model/runtime assets.
For a fully air-gapped deployment, host these locally and set `wasm_paths` (and a
local `model`) in the plugin config; `tts.js` will point the runtime at them.

## Reproducing the bundle

```
npm init -y && npm i kokoro-js@1.2.1
printf 'export * from "kokoro-js";\nexport { env } from "@huggingface/transformers";\n' > entry.mjs
npx esbuild entry.mjs --bundle --minify --format=esm --platform=browser --target=es2022 --outfile=kokoro.min.js
```

`voices.json` is regenerated by reading kokoro-js's `KokoroTTS.prototype.voices`
getter (a static map; it needs no model load).
